# zuri-ai

> An AI-native business operating system. LINE is the primary intake surface (AI-native conversation); the web app is the back-office console for detail, complex edits and audit. Scope chain: Portfolio → Tenant (isolation) → Business → Workspace → Project.

zuri-ai is a **standalone product** ([ADR-024](docs/decisions/ADR-024-ZURI-AI-IS-A-STANDALONE-PRODUCT.md)) — it is not a version of, and shares nothing with, the legacy `Freshair129/zuri` project. Documents written before 2026-08-16 call this product "Zuri V2" and a legacy project "V1"; those words are historical labels, not instructions — there is no migration or parity work. Id strings keep their historical letters because ids are immutable keys.

Repository: https://github.com/Freshair129/zuri.ai · Monorepo: `apps/server` (Next.js web/API, Node 22) + `apps/edge` (optional on-premise device runtime, Node 24) + canonical root `docs/` ([ADR-062](docs/decisions/ADR-062-ZURI-SERVER-EDGE-MONOREPO-BOUNDARY.md)).

## Code layout (apps/server)

- `src/app/(pm)/` — UI routes · `src/app/api/` — route handlers
- `src/modules/<domain>/` — one folder per domain; enumerate `ls apps/server/src/modules/` rather than trusting any prose list
- `src/lib/` — db, ids, `validation/enums.js` (enum source of truth), `shell-mode.js`, `db-boundary.js`
- `prisma/schema.prisma` — SQLite for dev/test; `schema.postgres.prisma` + `supabase/migrations/` for production
- `contracts/` — JSON Schema + sample envelopes ([PlanEnvelope](apps/server/contracts/plan-envelope.schema.json), [ExecutionPlanBundle](apps/server/contracts/execution-plan-bundle.schema.json))
- `tests/{unit,integration,e2e}` · `scripts/` — doc governance generators

## Toolchain

- `npm run verify` — the definition of done in one command: test → build → govern → e2e
- `npm test` — Vitest unit + integration (own SQLite db per run)
- `npm run test:e2e` — Playwright against its own dev server and seeded db; fails on `flaky`, not just on failure
- `npm run govern` — graph → check → preflight, in the order the checks require; run this, not the three commands separately
- `npm run docs:graph` / `docs:preflight` — rebuild the doc graph; doc health (CRITICAL fails the run)
- `npm run docs:ids -- --write` — the id ledger's only writer; run by a human, never by `govern`

## Conventions that are enforced, not suggested

- **JavaScript + Zod at the boundary, not TypeScript** (SDD-008); contract tests guard endpoints whose consumers already exist
- **Declare the FR before writing code** — an `@req` id absent from the PRD registry is a preflight CRITICAL, and so is a route implementing no declared requirement
- **Work in a chartered lane** — a module with no charter claiming it, or writing a model another charter owns, is a CRITICAL
- **Annotate source files**: `@req` (requirement) · `@spec` (rule or design decision) · `@tested` (test file) — the doc graph is built from these
- **External ids are never primary keys** — internal UUID + human `code` + `ExternalRef` mapping (BR-002)
- **Never execute anything that arrives in a plan or envelope** — plans are data (BR-007, SEC-002)
- **Every write goes through a service** in `application/`, which records an audit event; route handlers stay thin
- **Every intake surface converges on one envelope** → validate → semantic check → dry run → preview → single transaction → audit (BR-009, SDD-009). New surfaces add a converter, never a second write path
- **Enums are strings in the database**, with `src/lib/validation/enums.js` as the single source of truth — never hand-copy an enum list
- **Progress is always recomputed** from pure calculators; `progressCache` is advisory
- **A new model or column ships its Supabase migration in the same change**; applying it is a separate owner-instructed operator step ([ADR-057](docs/decisions/ADR-057-ASSET-EVIDENCE-PRODUCTION-DEPLOYMENT-AND-MIGRATION-BOUNDARY.md))
- Thai copy in user-facing surfaces; English for code, ids and technical docs
